result.summary: Independently re-derived (not copied from TEST-RUNNER's step-04 report) all 7 of REQ-151's acceptance_criteria against the real current code/tests on feature/WF02-REQ151-20260826, and independently re-ran scripts/test_parallel.sh myself (fresh `mix deps.get` + clean `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`, 0 warnings). AC1: `grep -rn "Lua.new(" lib --include=*.ex` returns exactly one line, `lib/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox.ex:206`, matching sandbox_test.exs's 'Lua.new( appears exactly once under lib/, inside sandbox.ex' test. AC2: sandbox_test.exs's 'per-path denials (AC2)' describe block individually evaluates and calls io.open, io.write, os.execute, os.exit, os.getenv, os.remove, os.rename, os.tmpname, load, loadfile, dofile, require, package, and debug (each assert_raise Lua.RuntimeException), plus string.dump asserted nil -- all 14 named surfaces present, ran clean. AC3: 'default denials hold' describe block asserts os.execute and load stay denied both via Sandbox.new/0 and via Sandbox.new/1 with an arbitrary/unrecognized opts keyword list, guarding the :sandboxed-replaces-defaults trap; moduledoc's '## No custom deny-set list' section states no custom list is exposed and names REQ-152 as the requirement that adds one (confirmed present, 'names REQ-152' test passes). AC4: moduledoc's 'LUA-03 restatement' section states all three reasons verbatim -- (a) loadstring is a Lua 5.1 name absent from 5.3, (b) jit/ffi/bit do not exist in Lua 5.3 (vacuous), (c) SBX-1's open-then-prune ordering does not transfer as a mechanism -- and 3 moduledoc-content tests assert on these exact substrings ('restates LUA-03's loadstring-absent-from-5.3 reason', '...jit/ffi/bit vacuity reason', '...SBX-1 property-not-mechanism reason'), all pass. AC5: moduledoc's 'LUA-04 restatement' section states the runtime has no bytecode loader, holds structurally, no rejection path to test; 'restates LUA-04's structural-holds text' test asserts on 'LUA-04'/'bytecode'/'structurally', passes. AC6: @sandbox_deny_set (sandbox.ex:112-182) lists 28 explicit {path, reason} tuples each with a per-entry reason string (verified by direct read, counted: 14 io.* + file + 6 os.* + package/load/loadfile/require/dofile/loadstring + debug = 28); moduledoc's '## coroutine decision' section records the explicit decision (no deny-set entry added, reasoned) and its rationale; 'records the coroutine decision and its reason' test passes. AC7: `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` exit 0 / no output; REQ-151's own suite (sandbox_test.exs + lua_script_audit_test.exs) standalone: 'Result: 46 passed'. Independently re-ran scripts/test_parallel.sh myself (N=8, source: nproc): combined 2057 tests, 5 properties, 2 failures (2060/2062 passed) -- both failures in partition 1, test/docs/requirement_status_invariants_test.exs A5 and A4a (identical ISS-0332 vocabulary-drift failure at docs/status/requirement_status.v4.yaml:1122). Re-derived attribution myself rather than trusting step-04's report: confirmed `git diff --name-only main...HEAD` touches only handoffs/, lib/letflow/design/req151-lua-sandbox.md, lib/letflow/engine/lua/sandbox.ex, mix.exs/mix.lock, test/letflow/engine/lua/{sandbox_test.exs,lua_script_audit_test.exs}, test/reports/, test/specs/REQ-151.md -- no docs/status/ file in the diff -- and independently reproduced the identical A5/A4a failure in a fresh worktree checked out at merge-base 8c331b6621becb11814a0cc234411527e2e21db5 (own mix deps.get + mix test run, not copied from step-04's log): 'Result: 18/20 passed, Failed: 2 tests', same ISS-0332/line 1122 signature. Confirmed structurally pre-existing and unrelated to REQ-151's diff. F3 (context_test.exs flake) from step-04's report did not reproduce in my run at all (2 failures, not 3) -- consistent with step-04's own characterization of it as intermittent/non-reproducing, and it does not affect this verdict either way since it also traces to no file in this branch's diff. All 7 acceptance criteria independently verified against real code/tests; both observed test failures are independently re-confirmed pre-existing and out of REQ-151's scope. Also confirmed via docs/requirements.yaml that REQ-151's acceptance_criteria list is unchanged from what TEST-DESIGNER/TEST-RUNNER worked against, and that this is a WF-02 (not stage-gate) run so no docs/migration/stage-N sign-off section applies.
